the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-0: Suetonius gives us the old world's most ill-famed portrait of a mad king. Young Gaius Caligula ruled Rome for just four years, calling himself a living god, wasting the gold in the vaults, and striking fear into the Senate until knives ended him in 41 AD. Set down a lifetime later from court talk and state papers, the life is as gripping as it is shocking.
ideala: Sarah Grand — the firebrand of the New Woman movement — creates in Ideala a heroine who thinks for herself about marriage, morality, and women's rights. The novel challenged Victorian conventions and made its author famous. A bold, important voice from the dawn of modern feminism.
a-woman-s-life-work-labors-and-experienc: Laura Haviland of Michigan tells of her life-work — hiding runaways, teaching freed folk, and a long life of kind deeds. Her plain tale both shames and lifts the heart. The true story of a brave, good woman. Her courage helped bend a nation's conscience toward justice.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abila: This 1913 reference piece on Abila — the name of several ancient towns, in Syria and beyond. The entry sorts the sites with care. Lysanias of Abilene ruled one of them. Geography for students of the Gospels. Luke's Gospel names its tetrarch in passing.
